chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from his father, from Abu Maryam who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the charity of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the charity of Ali (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for us (peace be upon him).' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Fatima (peace be upon her) made her charity to be for the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib.'

key_terms.صَدَقَة: Charity (general alms, distinct from zakat in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the Imams consuming sadaqah and how did Fatima designate her charity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the distinct legal status of the Prophet’s and Imams’ charity (*sadaqah*) compared to general *zakat*, affirming its permissibility for the Ahl al-Bayt as a divine privilege. It specifically notes Fatima’s designation of her charity for the clans of Hashim and al-Muttalib, highlighting the intra-family distribution of charitable wealth that distinguishes their status from the broader Muslim community. This ruling underscores the theological and jurisprudential autonomy of the Imams in managing religious endowments.
